questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

When he heard that he had got admission in IIT, he was _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**on top of the world"**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **on top of the world **- This idiom means **to feel extremely happy or elated as if one is at the highest point of happiness and success.**

 
 
• **An example sentence would be**, *"When he heard that he had got admission in IIT, he was on top of the world, he couldn't believe that his dream has come true."*
 
• It is often used to describe a sense of accomplishment or success as if one is at the highest point of happiness and success.
 
• **For example,** if someone has achieved a long-term goal or dream, they might say "I feel on top of the world" to express the feeling of happiness and contentment that comes from achieving something important.__
 
 

**Hence, the correct answer is** *"on top of the world"*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**** Let's see the meaning of the other given idioms.**

__
 
• **"On the ball"** is an idiomatic phrase that is used to describe someone who is well-prepared, efficient, and capable__.

 __
 
• *** *****For example,***** **if someone is able to handle a difficult situation well, they might be described as "being on the ball." *
 
• It is a positive term and can be used to appreciate someone's ability to handle things in an efficient and effective way.
 
 
 
• **"On the ropes" i**s an idiom that is used to describe someone who is in a difficult or precarious situation.__ 
 __
 
• **For example,* ****if someone is in a difficult financial situation, they might say "I'm on the ropes" to express the feeling of being in a difficult or precarious position*.
 
• It is the **opposite of being on top of the world.**
 
 
 
• **"On the hot seat"** is an idiomatic phrase that is used to describe someone who is in a difficult or uncomfortable situation, particularly one in which they are being closely questioned or scrutinized. __
 
 
• **For example,* ****if someone is being questioned by the authorities, they might be described as "being on the hot seat."*
 
• It is a negative term, and it can indicate that someone is under pressure or in a difficult situation that they would rather not be in.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given proverb.

A watched pot never boils

options.text: Everything ends; good times don’t last forever
It’s better to finish something late than to never do it at all
Something we wait for with impatient attention seems to take forever.
Don’t expect a positive result before you actually see it

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Something we wait for with impatient attention seems to take forever.** '

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• A watched pot never boils is proverb that means **i****f something takes time to do, it doesn’t help to constantly check on it. You just have to give it time.**

 
 
• ​Example - I know you think he’s going to be a great guitar player one day, but stop criticizing him so much. He just started taking lessons two weeks ago! **A watched pot never boils.**
 
 
 
• So, **something we wait for with impatient attention seems to take forever** is the most appropriate meaning of the given proverb.
 
• Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• A watched pot never boils - एक अंतहीन इंतज़ार
 
• कहने का मतलब यह है कि यदि आप किसी चीज़ को घटित होते देखने के लिए उत्सुकता से प्रतीक्षा करते रहेंगे और देखते रहेंगे, तो ऐसा प्रतीत होगा कि इसमें बहुत लंबा समय लगेगा, या यह बिल्कुल भी घटित नहीं होगा।

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Pull the plug is an idiom that means **to do something that prevents an activity from continuing, especially by no longer giving money to support it.** 

 
 
• ​Example - *If the viewing figures drop much more, the TV network will probably **pull the plug **on the whole series.*
 
 
 
• So, end something is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
 
• Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the correct meaning of the idiom given.

Cut no ice

options.text: Have no influence or effect on
Feel too cold to do anything

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Have no influence or effect on"**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• "Cut no ice" is an idiomatic expression that means have no influence or effect on. ("कट नो आइस" एक मुहावरेदार अभिव्यक्ति है जिसका अर्थ है कि कोई प्रभाव नहीं है।)
 
 
• ***For example,** "I tried to explain my point of view to the boss, but it cut no ice and he still made the decision that he wanted."*
 
 

**Let's see the meanings of the given words**__

__
 
• **"Feel sorry for someone"** refers to feeling compassion or sympathy for someone who is in a difficult situation. ("किसी के लिए खेद महसूस करें" किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति के लिए करुणा या सहानुभूति महसूस करने को संदर्भित करता है जो कठिन परिस्थिति में है।)

 
 
• ***For example, **"I couldn't help but **feel sorry for** the homeless man on the street corner."*
 
 
 
• **"Have no influence or effect on" **refers to the lack of ability to change or impact a situation or person. It means that something or someone has no power to affect or sway the outcome. ("कोई प्रभाव नहीं है" किसी स्थिति या व्यक्ति को बदलने या प्रभावित करने की क्षमता की कमी को संदर्भित करता है। इसका अर्थ है कि किसी वस्तु या व्यक्ति के पास परिणाम को प्रभावित करने की शक्ति नहीं है।)
 
 
• ***For example,** "I tried to convince my friend to change his mind, but my words had **no influence or effect **on him." *
 
 
 
• **"Feel too cold to do anything**" refers to a physical feeling of being too cold to function or move. ("कुछ भी करने के लिए बहुत ठंडा महसूस करें" कार्य करने या स्थानांतरित करने के लिए कोई रूचि नहीं है इस भावना को संदर्भित करता है।)
 
 
• ***For example, **"It was so cold outside, I felt **too cold to do anything **but stay inside."*
 
 
 
• **"Have a good influence on"** refers to having a positive impact or effect on someone or something. ("किसी पर अच्छा प्रभाव है" का अर्थ किसी व्यक्ति या किसी चीज़ पर सकारात्मक प्रभाव या प्रभाव होना है।)
 
 
• ***For example,** "My mentor's guidance had a **good influence **on my professional development."*
 
 

**According to the meanings of the given words,** *the correct answer is **Option 2, i.e., Have no influence or effect on.***

options.text: to do something difficult in a determined and confident way
to run away at the slightest sign of danger

questions.solution:
The right answer is '**to do something difficult in a determined and confident way'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Take the bull by the horns**- deal decisively with a difficult or dangerous situation.

 **E.g.**__- She decided to **take the bull by the horns** and organize things for herself.

Hence, the correct answer is '**Option (1)**'**.**
